hero.oneLiner: Mumbai-based film production house that originates, develops, produces, markets and distributes Hindi films, web series and TV serials, monetising the resulting intellectual property across theatrical, OTT, television and music rights.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mumbai-based film production house that originates, develops, produces, markets and distributes Hindi films, web series and TV serials, monetising the resulting intellectual property across theatrical, OTT, television and music rights.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 2007 (originally 'Energetic Films Private Limited'), Sunshine Pictures is a production house engaged in originating, creating, developing, producing, marketing and distributing films, TV serials and web series, either as sole producer (retaining all rights and upside) or as co-producer with studios for a fixed fee plus a retained share of IP and profit. As on the date of the RHP it has produced thirteen commercial films (seven co-produced, six self-produced), two web series, three TV serials and one short film, with 'The Kerala Story' described in the commissioned D&B Report as the highest return-on-investment blockbuster of 2023. It has recently added two verticals, Sunshine Music (in-house music label) and Sunshine Digital (Originals), and sells to studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- De Novo Cinematics Private Limited (formerly De Novo Hospitality Private Limited) — Group Company (sole Group Company as on the date of the RHP): Incorporated September 20, 2021; CIN U59111MH2021PTC367795; registered at Kandivli East, Mumbai. RHP states it has no interest in the promotion of the Company, no common pursuits, and no pending litigation with material impact on the Company.
- Subsidiaries — None: RHP affirmatively states: 'As on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus, our Company does not have any subsidiaries.' (Note: FY25 and FY24 financials are presented on a consolidated basis, FY26 on a standalone basis.)
- Vipul Amrutlal Shah (individual, Promoter) — Related party - lessor, lender and deposit counterparty: Lessor of the Registered Office at Rs 8,00,000 per month; has sanctioned Rs 1,100 lakhs of working capital funding to the Company; Company carries a Rs 150.00 lakhs refundable deposit receivable from him (0.84% of total assets as on March 31, 2026); has issued personal/corporate guarantee for ICICI Bank working capital facility of Rs 820.00 lakhs (Rs 271.16 lakhs outstanding as on March 31, 2026).
- Miracle Movies — Related party: Company extended loans and advances of Rs 206.63 lakhs as on March 31, 2026, constituting 1.15% of total assets; also shown as recipient of a security deposit of Rs 160.00 lakhs in a prior year.
- Solarya Hospitality Private Limited (formerly Sunshine Ark Hospitality Private Limited) — Promoter Group / entity where Whole-time Directors Aryaman and Maurya Vipul Shah are directors: Advance of Rs 50.00 lakhs received against sale of asset held for sale.
- Solarya Habitats Private Limited — Other directorship of Whole-time Directors Aryaman Vipul Shah and Maurya Vipul Shah
- Shefali Shah Creations (OPC) Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoter and Whole-time Director Shefali Vipul Shah

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Production and distribution of films and associated rights:** Theatrical feature films (sole-produced and co-produced), Released titles include Force, Commando: A One-Man Army, Holiday: A soldier is never off duty, Force 2, Commando 2, Commando 3, Sanak, The Kerala Story, Governor: The Silent Saviour (released June 12, 2026), FY26 revenue Rs 6,675.72 lakhs (89.68% of revenue from operations); FY25 Rs 5,380.70 lakhs (52.08%); FY24 Rs 13,083.38 lakhs (97.78%)
- **Production and distribution of web series / TV serials and associated rights:** Web series (two produced; maiden digital original 'Bawra Mann' and 'Ankahee' on Sunshine Digital), TV serials (three produced), FY26 revenue Rs 98.50 lakhs (1.32%); FY25 Rs 4,950.00 lakhs (47.90%); FY24 Rs 275.34 lakhs (2.06%)
- **Others:** Music rights exploitation and in-house music label (Sunshine Music; 36 original music videos on YouTube), Talent management, Social media platforms (YouTube 1,96,000 subscribers, Instagram 1,32,000 followers, Facebook 1,06,000), FY26 revenue Rs 669.45 lakhs (8.99%); FY25 Rs 2.32 lakhs (0.02%); FY24 Rs 21.08 lakhs (0.16%)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Theatrical box office (Indian cinema, Hindi-language films)
- OTT / streaming platforms and digital originals (e.g. web series produced for Amazon Seller Services Private Limited)
- Satellite / television broadcast rights
- Music rights, music streaming and digital/social platforms (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook)
- Overseas markets for Indian films and web series (RHP notes limited global penetration; operations concentrated in India)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Vertically integrated content originator rather than a manufacturer: the Company states it engages in 'research & development of scripts, end-to-end production of content, intellectual property creation, monetization of rights and distribution'. Production runs from conceptualization and scripting, through cast/crew finalisation, a cost-of-production budget covering pre-production, production and post-production, and a separate Print and Advertising (P&A) budget covering marketing and distribution. Editing is generally carried out in-house 'for creative reasons'; dubbing, sound and VFX are outsourced to different studios/professionals while closely monitored. Post-production capability is described as digital intermediate (DI) colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines. Two operating models: (i) co-production with a reputable studio, where the Company produces for a fixed fee plus a share of the intellectual property and profits, giving 'certainty in earnings' and de-risking cashflows; and (ii) sole production, where the Company finances the entire project and retains all rights - intellectual property, titles and distribution rights - allowing it to keep the entire theatrical upside and monetise OTT, music rights and downstream derivatives (remakes, sequels/prequels, spin-offs, dubbings, foreign-language renditions, stage plays, web series and television production). Forward channel is via renowned studios, independent distributors, OTT platforms and broadcasters, plus the Company's own social media presence (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook). Backward integration is deliberately light: 'Since we are not a manufacturing company, details of raw materials are not applicable to us'; equipment (cameras, lights, grips, picture vehicles, setting equipment) is rented from third-party local players, while the Company uses its own editing equipment; power is drawn from the local grid supplemented by hired diesel generator sets at shooting sites; water is required only for drinking and sanitary purposes. Cost control measures include a no-cash / minimum-cash payment policy with payments through banking channels and on-set accountants to manage payments, track daily expenses and audit. The Company states it has not entered into any collaboration or joint venture 'except collaborating with other producers in the ordinary course of business on specific film projects'. Human resources: 28 full-time employees on roll as on June 2026 (Accounts and Finance 5, Admin 12, Business Development 8 including Executive Directors, IT 1, Compliance 1, HR 1), with approximately 150-300 skilled professionals and unskilled labour engaged per project over the production journey. Intellectual property is protected by copyright (registration optional in India) and by trademark applications: 'SUNSHINE PICTURES' application 6643047 (class 41) Accepted & Advertised, 6643048 (class 43) Abandoned, 6643049 (class 41) Objected, 6643050 (class 43) Abandoned, all applied September 26, 2024; and seven device-mark applications dated July 15, 2026 (7120962, 7120964, 7120967, 7120968, 7120969 - formalities check pass; 7120963, 7120965 - objected), all class 41. The Company also states it has no outstanding export obligations.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue is lumpy and project-timing driven: FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 7,443.67 lakhs against Rs 10,333.01 lakhs in FY25 and Rs 13,379.80 lakhs in FY24, with FY25 benefiting from an exceptionally strong base and FY26 described as a normalised base in which fewer projects reached revenue-recognition milestones; large projects under production are scheduled for release in Fiscal 2026-27 with revenue to be recognised in later periods.
- Content cost sits in inventory until release: operational cost fell 73.27% to Rs 1,362.50 lakhs in FY26 from Rs 5,097.53 lakhs in FY25 because a significant portion of production spend on ongoing projects remained in closing inventory pending release or revenue recognition - which flatters reported FY26 Operating EBITDA margin (76.61% vs 46.72% in FY25).
- Working capital cycle is the dominant cash driver: net working capital of Rs 12,646.25 lakhs as on March 31, 2026 equal to 169.89% of revenue from operations, versus Rs 7,298.19 lakhs (70.63%) at March 31, 2025 and Rs 5,103.24 lakhs (38.14%) at March 31, 2024; project gestation from inception is generally 6 to 18 months and credit periods are given to distributors and OTT platforms.
- Operating cash flow turned negative in FY26 at Rs (3,320.63) lakhs against Rs 2,847.30 lakhs in FY25 and Rs 3,159.64 lakhs in FY24, attributed to higher inventory and trade receivables.
- Revenue mix shifts sharply between films and web series/TV serials year to year (films 89.68% of FY26 revenue vs 52.08% in FY25; web series/TV serials 1.32% vs 47.90%), while the 'Others' stream (music rights, talent management, social media) rose to 8.99% of FY26 revenue.
- Overhead build-up ahead of scale: employee benefit expenses rose 53.90% to Rs 208.36 lakhs in FY26 from Rs 135.39 lakhs in FY25 on induction of senior leadership and KMPs to support the growth pipeline.
- Other income is small and volatile: Rs 183.82 lakhs in FY26 against Rs 247.26 lakhs in FY25 (a 25.66% decrease), FY25 having benefited from fair-valuation and investment disposal gains and an E&O insurance claim.
- Low leverage: total borrowings of Rs 909.42 lakhs as on March 31, 2026 with a debt-equity ratio of 0.06 (0.11 in FY25, 0.24 in FY24), with working capital met from internal accruals, bank facilities and funding from the Promoter.
- Model mix determines earnings predictability: fixed-fee co-productions give contractually assured minimum consideration at stages of completion regardless of box office, while sole productions carry full risk but retain theatrical upside and downstream OTT, satellite, music and derivative rights.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Increase production capacity - expand the writer pool and commission more story ideas to build a bigger script funnel, and hire and groom young creative talent to build a leadership bench so multiple projects across formats can run concurrently.
- Diversify the portfolio - produce a wider genre mix (drama, thriller, comedy, biopics, historical fiction, socially relevant cinema, family entertainment) across theatrical, direct-to-OTT, web series, short films and TV serials to broaden the audience base and improve revenue predictability.
- Scale the music vertical - grow Sunshine Music by acquiring and distributing music rights, creating original audio content and leveraging digital music platforms.
- Launch new businesses - invest in adjacencies within and around the production value chain such as studios, outsourced VFX and post-production services, and build a content library over a three-to-five-year period to generate a steady revenue stream.
- Embrace new-age media - hire talent, build partnerships and leverage the content library to participate in AR/VR, mobile-first and digital convergence opportunities, and use audience data to shape content.
- Grow with structural industry drivers - rising screen count and Hindi-market penetration in Tier 2/Tier 3 cities, OTT subscriber growth, and expanding overseas demand including non-diaspora local audiences.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: There is no manufacturing capacity expansion; expansion is of content-production capacity and new verticals. The Company plans to gradually increase the number of projects produced every year over the medium and long term by widening its script-sourcing funnel (larger writer pool, more commissioned story ideas) and by hiring and grooming young creative talent so that multiple projects across formats can be executed concurrently, extending the revenue pipeline and improving medium-term visibility. It has recently launched two new verticals - Sunshine Music (in-house music label) and Sunshine Digital (Originals) - which are live with 36 original music videos and the digital web series 'Bawra Mann' and 'Ankahee', and intends to enter adjacencies such as studios, outsourced VFX and post-production services while building a content library over a three-to-five-year horizon. Immediate slate: 'Hisaab' (co-production with Jio Studios, in post-production, release scheduled Fiscal 2027), 'Samuk' (sole production, principal photography from August 2026, release Fiscal 2027) and the web series 'Nanavati vs Nanavati' for Amazon Seller Services (principal photography from July 20, 2026), with six films and two web series further in the pipeline scheduled between Fiscal 2028 and Fiscal 2029. The Fresh Issue funds this scale-up indirectly: up to Rs 11,250.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked for long-term working capital against an estimated Fiscal 2027 working capital requirement of Rs 32,049.37 lakhs, plus General Corporate Purposes.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Experienced Promoters supported by a senior management team - Promoter and MD Vipul Amrutlal Shah has over 25 years in the industry (director of 'Aankhen', 'Waqt', 'Namastey London', 'London Dreams'); VP-Production Aashin A. Shah has over 18 years and COO Ravichand Govind Nallappa over 25 years of industry experience.
- Established track record and long-standing relationships - 18 years of operating experience, thirteen commercial films, two web series, three TV serials and one short film produced; repeat business from top studios and distributors and access to top writing, acting, directing and music talent.
- Differentiated and de-risked business model - a portfolio blending fixed-fee co-productions (assured revenue and earnings visibility regardless of box office, with retained IP and profit share) and sole productions (full upside plus downstream OTT, satellite, music and derivative rights).
- Prudential cost approach - lean overheads, in-house story development, on-set accountants and a no-cash/minimum-cash payment policy; talent compensated partly through profit share so creative-talent cost as a percentage of production cost is stated to be among the lowest in the industry.
- Portfolio risk cap - exposure to any individual project limited to 30% of total annual budget.
- High-quality, technology-driven production standards - fully digitised workflow, DI colour grading, high-resolution editing suites, Dolby Atmos sound mixing and VFX pipelines, with data-driven greenlighting using audience analytics, genre trends, regional viewership and OTT consumption data.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Hit-driven, project-based revenue with no predictability of audience acceptance — The RHP states success is primarily dependent on audience acceptance which cannot be accurately predicted, and that the business model is project-based with inherently volatile revenue streams. Revenue from operations swung from Rs 13,379.80 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 10,333.01 lakhs (FY25) to Rs 7,443.67 lakhs (FY26) purely on release and revenue-recognition timing.
- Extreme customer concentration on a handful of studios and independent distributors, whose names are not disclosed — Top 5 customers contributed Rs 5,568.60 lakhs or 74.81% of revenue in FY26, Rs 10,315.59 lakhs or 99.83% in FY25 and Rs 11,117.33 lakhs or 83.09% in FY24; the single largest customer was 26.87% of FY26 revenue and 47.90% of FY25 revenue. The Company states it cannot disclose customer names for want of their consent, and the top-5 set varies year to year.
- Working capital intensity and negative operating cash flow — Net working capital of Rs 12,646.25 lakhs at March 31, 2026 equals 169.89% of revenue from operations (up from 70.63% in FY25 and 38.14% in FY24); projects take 6 to 18 months from inception and cash outflows on cast, crew, locations and equipment precede revenue. Operating cash flow was Rs (3,320.63) lakhs in FY26. Rs 11,250.00 lakhs of Net Proceeds is earmarked for working capital against an estimated FY27 requirement of Rs 32,049.37 lakhs.
- Key-man and Promoter dependence, with a Promoter Group holding near-total pre-Offer control — The Company is led by Promoter and MD Vipul Amrutlal Shah, who also directs its films, leases it the Registered Office, has lent it Rs 1,100 lakhs and guarantees its bank facility. The four Promoters together hold 99.99% of pre-Offer equity and the RHP flags that they will jointly retain majority control post-Offer, which may lead to decisions in conflict with other shareholders.
- Litigation and regulatory overhang, including a criminal complaint by the Registrar of Companies over past financial statements — The Assistant Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra has filed a criminal miscellaneous application (No. 687 of 2025) against the Company, Vipul Amrutlal Shah, Shefali Vipul Shah and two others alleging contraventions relating to accounting treatments and disclosures in past financial statements, adjourned to September 17, 2026. Direct and indirect tax proceedings against the Company involve Rs 3,174.42 lakhs across 8 cases, and contingent liabilities stood at Rs 3,172.96 lakhs as on March 31, 2026 (including a Rs 1,882.19 lakhs income-tax demand for AY 2020-21 and a Rs 1,290.27 lakhs service-tax demand).
- Asset-light with no owned production hardware and premises largely leased, including from the Promoter — The RHP states the Company does not own the hardware or equipment required for content production and does not own the premises of its Registered Office and storage facility; the Registered Office is leased from Promoter Vipul Amrutlal Shah at Rs 8,00,000 per month under a lease running only to March 31, 2027, so any adverse change in that arrangement or in third-party equipment availability could disrupt production.
- Content risk: censorship, objectionable-content backlash and piracy — Films require Central Board of Film Certification clearance, viewers or civil society organisations may find content objectionable (a live issue for a producer of socially and politically charged titles such as 'The Kerala Story'), and unauthorised distribution or piracy could erode revenues from titles whose economic life is short.
- Related-party dependence and receivables from related parties — The Company funds working capital partly from the Promoter, carries a Rs 150.00 lakhs refundable deposit receivable from Vipul Amrutlal Shah (0.84% of total assets) and Rs 206.63 lakhs of loans and advances to Miracle Movies (1.15% of total assets) as on March 31, 2026, and states it may continue entering related-party transactions.
